references.text: The leper had to live outside the camp, which explains why the priest must go out of the camp to examine him.
Confirms that lepers were to be sent outside the camp to keep it clean.
Miriam became leprous and had to stay outside the camp for seven days, an example of the practice of this law.
Four leprous men sat at the city gate, outside the community, in accordance with the law requiring residence outside the camp.
Jesus healed a leper and sent him to the priest to show himself, as prescribed by the law in Leviticus.
Jesus healed a leper and commanded him to show himself to the priest and offer what Moses had commanded.
Jesus healed a leper and sent him to the priest to follow the cleansing ritual of the Mosaic Law.
The ten lepers stood at a distance (outside the community), and Jesus sent them to the priests to be declared clean.
